title: Flower Clouds
medium: Pastel, with touches of stumping, incising, and brushwork, on blue-gray wove paper with multi-colored fibers altered to tan, perimeter mounted to cardboard

altText: A dreamlike pastel drawing of two figures in a sailboat floating beneath glowing, bright multicolored clouds that look like giant flowers.

context: A pastel drawing made in France around 1903 by Odilon Redon, an artist who first worked only in black and white and then turned to color through pastel in the 1890s. The Art Institute describes two figures in a sailboat beneath bright, multicolored clouds, in a glowing, dreamlike scene.

descriptions.k: Two people are in a little boat. Above them are glowing clouds in bright colors that look like flowers. It is like a dream. Can you find the boat? What colors do you see in the sky?
descriptions.g12: Odilon Redon drew a dream. Two figures sail in a little boat under clouds that glow like giant flowers. He used soft colored chalk called pastel. What do you think is it like to sail through that sky?
descriptions.g35: Odilon Redon made this pastel drawing in France around 1903. Two figures sit in a sailboat under bright, many-colored clouds that glow like flowers. At first Redon worked only in black and white, but later he fell in love with color. Why might he make a picture that feels like a dream?
descriptions.g68: Odilon Redon's Flower Clouds (c. 1903) shows two figures in a sailboat under glowing, multicolored clouds. Redon first worked in black and white and turned to color through pastel in the 1890s. The scene feels like a dream rather than a real place. How do color and soft pastel strokes create a mood that real life rarely offers?
descriptions.g910: In Flower Clouds (c. 1903), Odilon Redon places two figures in a sailboat beneath luminous, multicolored clouds, a dreamlike vision rendered in pastel. After years of working in black and white, Redon found in pastel a way to make color glow. The image resists a single story. What does a work gain, and risk, when it invites feeling and imagination more than explanation?
descriptions.g1112: Redon's Flower Clouds (c. 1903) suspends two sailing figures within glowing, multicolored clouds, an image that reads as vision rather than description. Having worked first in black and white, Redon turned to pastel in the 1890s, discovering color as a medium of suggestion. As a Symbolist work, it favors mood and dream over narrative. How does the picture make ambiguity productive, and what is the relationship between inner vision and visible form?

teacherNote.context: A pastel drawing made in France around 1903 by Odilon Redon, an artist who first worked only in black and white and then turned to color through pastel in the 1890s. The Art Institute describes two figures in a sailboat beneath bright, multicolored clouds, in a glowing, dreamlike scene.
directions: Have students use chalk pastels on dark paper to create a dream sky and blend colors with their fingers.
Ask students to tell a short story about where the boat is going, then compare their stories.
Discuss how colors can express feelings or dreams instead of just copying real life.
